capabilities.target: GitHub repository branch and pull request, org-wide reach via token scope

capabilities.tool_ref: slack MCP post_message (planned, not yet built)

inputs.source: GitHub issue title and body, public repository

instructions.note: Any GitHub user can open an issue and apply the bug label through the repo's issue template (runtime notes), yet the prompt treats that label alone as sufficient authorization for full, unattended action including code execution and pushing branches with a broadly scoped credential.
'Fix it end to end' and 'run whatever commands you need' place no bound on the means the agent may use to satisfy an attacker-labeled task.

The only control against destructive or exfiltrating commands is a prompt instruction. Shell access, unrestricted network, and a broad credential in the environment make the forbidden actions fully available to a sufficiently persuaded or capable model.
Defense against instructions embedded in issues or code is purely behavioral and is the only mitigation named for indirect prompt injection.

The agent is explicitly authorized to edit its own .agent/config.yaml (tools, autonomy, network, credentials) whenever it judges it needs to, with no approval gate and no file permission boundary. This is a self-modification capability granted directly by the system prompt, matching the TC3 pattern.

elements.name: GitHub (public repo and org repos reachable by the token)
Shared CI runner container executing issue-fixer
Planned Slack MCP server (next quarter, not yet connected)

controls.name: Prompt rule forbidding destructive or exfiltrating commands
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing not to run destructive or exfiltrating commands. A more capable or adversarially prompted model rationalizes exceptions or splits the forbidden action into steps that individually look benign.

controls.name: Prompt rule to ignore instructions found in issues or code
controls.decay_rationale: Only holds if the model reliably distinguishes task content from instructions within that content. Adaptive, multi-step injections close this gap as model capability rises.

controls.name: Enumerated tool list in .agent/config.yaml
controls.decay_rationale: The listed tools (shell.run, fs.write, fs.read, github.push_branch, github.open_pr) do not themselves restrict what shell.run can execute or what fs.write can touch, and the agent can rewrite this very list via cap.self_config. It provides no credit against the exfiltration or self-modification paths found in this assessment; it is recorded for completeness and because it fails further under new_tool and new_mcp_server triggers.

controls.name: Container isolation on a shared CI runner
controls.decay_rationale: Isolates the host OS, but network is unrestricted and the org-wide PAT is mounted as an environment variable inside the container, so the sandbox does not contain credential exfiltration or network egress (per control_decay.md: watch mounted secrets and network). No credit applies to the findings in this assessment.

controls.name: Egress allowlist (not present)
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. An egress allowlist restricted to the GitHub API and required package registries would sever token- and data-exfiltration paths that rely on arbitrary outbound network access from shell.run.

controls.name: Per-repo, least-privilege credential (not present)
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. The deployed token is an org-wide PAT with repo and workflow scope on all org repositories. A token scoped to only the triggering repository, with no workflow scope, would prevent confused-deputy access to unrelated repos.

controls.name: Human approval gate before push or PR (not present)
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. No approval gate exists before github.push_branch/open_pr or before shell execution triggered by externally-labeled issues.

controls.name: Read-only agent configuration (not present)
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Making .agent/config.yaml read-only to the agent's own runtime identity, with changes requiring a separate human-reviewed deployment path, would sever the self-modification path entirely.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted issue triggers shell exfiltration of the org-wide PAT

attack_path.note: Any GitHub user can open an issue and apply the bug label via the issue template, authoring attacker-controlled task content.
Agent treats the bug label as authorization to act fully autonomously (prompt.md:1) and runs attacker-directed commands to reproduce/test (prompt.md:2).
shell.run executes with network unrestricted and the org-wide GITHUB_TOKEN in its environment; a command can read and exfiltrate the token to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: model.name/version changes away from the pinned baseline (model: latest, swappable: true), or prompt.md lines 4-5 are edited or removed.

evidence.observation: Org-wide PAT with repo+workflow scope is present in the shell's environment, and network is set to unrestricted.
Agent is told to run whatever commands it needs against any issue labeled bug, with no scoping of who may label an issue.
Any GitHub user can open an issue and add the bug label through the issue template.

recommendations.action: Replace the org-wide PAT with a short-lived, repository-scoped token with no workflow scope, provisioned so shell.run cannot read it in cleartext.
Add an egress allowlist restricting outbound network from the container to the GitHub API and required package registries only.
Add outbound network logging/DLP scanning for credential-shaped strings in command output.

findings.title: Self-modification (TC3): prompt explicitly authorizes the agent to rewrite its own configuration

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled issue content frames a reason the agent would judge it needs extra tools.
Prompt explicitly authorizes editing .agent/config.yaml whenever the agent judges it needs more tools (prompt.md:6), with no approval gate.
fs.write targets .agent/config.yaml, able to add tools, widen autonomy, or alter env/network settings; the change persists and is inherited by every future run.

forecast.watch_signal: Diff .agent/config.yaml between runs; any autonomous change to tools, autonomy, network, or env fields without a human commit is the signal.

evidence.observation: Agent is explicitly told it may adjust .agent/config.yaml if it judges it needs extra tools.
fs.write is scoped to the whole workspace including .agent/, with no file permission boundary described.

recommendations.action: Mount .agent/config.yaml read-only to the agent's runtime identity; route configuration changes through a separate, human-approved deployment pipeline. Remove the prompt.md:6 permission.
Diff .agent/config.yaml between runs and alert on any change, treating any diff as an incident requiring review.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): org-wide PAT lets a single public-repo issue reach unrelated org repositories

attack_path.note: Attacker-authored issue in the public repository directs the agent to operate beyond the current repository.
Git operations using the org-wide PAT (repo+workflow scope on all org repos) can read confidential files from unrelated repositories.
github.push_branch/open_pr can expose data taken from other repos by pushing it into the public repo's branch or PR.

forecast.watch_signal: Any widening of PAT scope, or GitHub audit log entries showing this token accessing repositories other than the one that raised the triggering issue.

evidence.observation: Comment states the token has repo + workflow scope on all org repos, not just the current repository.
GitHub issue title/body is explicitly the public, untrusted trigger for this agent.

recommendations.action: Mint a fresh, fine-grained token per run scoped to only the repository that raised the triggering issue.
Add a destination confirmation bound to the system of record: allow pushes/PRs only to the originating repository.

findings.title: Forecast: planned Slack MCP server would add a new egress sink reachable by the same untrusted issue content

attack_path.note: The same untrusted issue content that already reaches shell and self-config would also reach any newly added Slack tool.
Planned Slack MCP tool (not yet built) would let the agent post messages or files to Slack channels, adding a new egress destination.

forecast.watch_signal: A Slack MCP server entry appears in deployment config or .agent/config.yaml tools list.

evidence.observation: Team wants to add a Slack MCP server next quarter; no manifest, auth method, or data scope is defined yet.

recommendations.action: Before connecting the Slack MCP server, pin and hash its tool definitions, verify peer identity, and restrict posting to a fixed, pre-approved channel with outbound content scrubbing for secrets.

rating.rationale: The agent accepts task content from a public repository (untrusted source) that any GitHub user can trigger, and operates with full unbounded autonomy, an org-wide PAT mounted in a shell with unrestricted network, and explicit prompt-level authorization to rewrite its own configuration. Inherent risk is critical across the credential-exfiltration, self-modification, and confused-deputy paths. The only present controls are two prompt instructions, both behavioral and dependent, plus a container sandbox and tool allowlist that do not actually restrict these specific paths; applying the one available credit (step 4, capped at one tier) yields a residual of high. A model upgrade, a prompt edit, or a longer task horizon removes the sole surviving controls and returns every present-day path to critical, and the planned Slack MCP integration would add a further egress channel at a comparable severity once connected.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, .agent/config.yaml, and the runtime notes provided; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior, verified actual GitHub token scopes, or live network egress rules.

No MCP/tool manifest or IaC was provided beyond .agent/config.yaml, so credential scope and network posture are taken as declared; whether 'network: unrestricted' and the PAT scope are enforced exactly as written at the container runtime level was not independently verified.

The planned Slack MCP server is described only at a roadmap level with no manifest, auth method, or data scope; the forecast finding for it is lower confidence and should be re-assessed once that integration is designed.

Repository file contents (in.repo_files) were rated untrusted based on the prompt's own acknowledgement that code may carry injected instructions; the actual contribution model (e.g., whether external pull requests are merged before the agent reads them) was not provided.
